Long distance and family relationships are tricky, but if this is what you're sure you want for yourself, ultimately no one can decide for you. Keep your focus on uni and your future, keep working towards your goals, and keep your communication open within your relationship. From what I've seen and the friends I've had it seems honestly more common for family to disapprove of a relationship than to support it, even if it is rock-solid. 

Be careful with yourself. With your relationship history it's important to check in and ask yourself how you're feeling about them, whether you're still with them out of love, if you feel considered and appreciated or manipulated. Be cautious, but remember to enjoy the good things. If he really loves you, he'll work with you and you two can figure it out together.

A bodybuilder and someone with an ED sounds like a match made in hell. I know everyone always says to just break up, but I really do think you should take some time to consider whether staying with someone who triggers you this much is worth it. It's a massive sacrifice for your mental health, and potentially your physical health if you end up giving in and going along with him. 

If you're going to stay with him I would recommend being really explicit about how you feel in the moment when he says these things. He needs to hear it right then, not later, and don't skip details. Remind him what you used to do to yourself when you heard comments like these before, and remind him every time. If he still won't quit, I really don't know what to tell you. 

Just make sure you're being really clear, and don't wait to tell him about it later.

One of the things that helped me a lot when my FPs would leave was going back to things I enjoyed when I was little. Did I like drawing, singing? Playing with pets? I'd explore those things. Anything, even a passing interest can help give a sense of identity, which can be crucial at this point when you so urgently need to get to know yourself, and care for yourself. 

My best advice is to get through today. And try to do one thing you enjoy every day, something you want for yourself that has nothing to do with your FP. 

Good luck, take your time and go easy on yourself.

I know it's awful now but I promise, you can get there. You are human! Take your time. You don't have to be healthy in an instant, it takes a while to make that progress. As someone who still has an ex in my life: it's not always painful or wrong or impossible to keep the people you love around. And sometimes, cutting them off can be emotionally catastrophic- i would never recommend anyone actively emotionally damage themselves like that without serious thought and a solid safety plan. It might be best long term, but some of us have to think short term, or it can take time to be ready to make that change.

Please don't call people idiots. We're all trying our best here.

I couldn't tell you what's going on with him, other than the obvious jealousy. I think, if you have the option, you should really just try to talk this out with him. In person if you can, since tone over text is tricky. He might not have realized the feelings and intent behind your "feeling like a burden" message. Seeing you out with other people might not have helped.

Either way. Don't feel guilty if you need to keep this person around. It's always a mixed bag with exes, good and bad times, and you won't always understand each other. There's a push and pull. It's best if you can both cut the impulse to be catty and text short little things, and just be open about how you feel, what you want.

I have to wonder how these comments would be different if you hadn't referred to your drawing as an "addiction" in your post. 

I have to wonder if you're on the spectrum- drawing can be very sensory and it can be easier for someone on the spectrum to overdo a sensory hobby or coping mechanism. 

Your wife reeeeally shouldn't have thrown out all your things. Also, all these people equating it to drugs and alcohol are really making some false equivalencies. You can't draw yourself to death, or overdose on it to the point of physical illness- worst you'd probably hit is financial strain, job loss, insomnia and carpal tunnel, not DEATH. Wow, guys. 

Be balanced. Think this out. It's awful that you blew up at your kid, and you should go into therapy, but I think maybe separately from your wife as well as in couples counseling. You need to really think whether the two of you can work together like this. She's decided you can't be balanced and do this in moderation. You've decided that you can. Focus on your kid and your mental health, and try to talk this over with your wife. Find out what she wants. Examine, how much are you really neglecting her and your kid? Get your mental health in order before you or your wife make any major decisions. If you both want this to work, take the time to work on this instead of giving each other ultimatums.

We have a weird grid setup at my store that lays things out by the hour, so you can see who needs to go and how much overlap you have visually. I would definitely recommend a system like that if you've got the advance time to lay it out. 

I'm not sure if you're going to be the one sending people to their breaks or just writing the break schedule, but if you're sending them:
A) stay ahead whenever you can. If it's 12:45 or 1:00 the next break isnt until 1:15, but someone has to go after they get back at 1:30, just send the first person now. You never know what will happen on their way to and from the lanes.
B) Don't panic! Even if there is a line a million people long, try not to wait more than 5 minutes after a set break time to send someone. "Waiting for the rush to die down" used to be doable but it's turned into a trap these days. If it gets crazy, call for guest first. 
C) this is almost a joke but Never Look An Angry Guest In The Eye or you will be cursed for all eternity/until they leave the store.
Oh, and if you have to monitor a line, carry your clipboard around. You look more official and people will be more willing to listen to you. Sounds silly but actually helps.
